profile.description: A STARTING POINT for a 16-core server, not a qualification. Every value here is either a property of the engine or a measured rule of thumb that held on more than one machine; the topology in particular must be re-measured on the target before any number from it is quoted.

hardware.cpu_family: any 16-core Arm server class (Neoverse N1/V1/V2 and equivalents)
hardware.notes: 16 physical cores without SMT is the shape this starting point assumes. On a cloud vCPU that is a HYPERTHREAD unless the instance was created with one thread per core, and with SMT on, eight threads means four real cores contending for the same FMA units -- which looks like the batching's fault and is not. Recreate the instance with one thread per core, or halve the thread split and re-measure.

requirements.blas: any OpenBLAS with a pthread build
requirements.kleidiai: vendored; the Arm matrix-unit paths are compiled and gated at runtime
requirements.note: GIT_REV must be passed on the command line: a synced tree has no .git, so the binary cannot certify its own commit.

server.worker_affinity: contiguous core slices, one per worker

precision.speech_decoder_weights: fp32 - QWEN_SD_INT8 is off by default and int4 measured slower on the first frame
precision.activations: fp32; int8 activations are quantized per call inside the int8 kernels
precision.gemm_backend: KleidiAI BFMMLA for bf16 matmat, SMMLA for int8 matmat, OpenBLAS sgemm for the speech decoder convolutions

OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT.why: MUST be set. Without it OpenBLAS idles by spinning and contends with the engine's own pool. Measured on this platform, same binary and bank, arms interleaved: first audio at concurrency 1 was 108 ms without it and 66 ms with it, and the bare arm was BIMODAL between the two, so one run lands on either and looks definitive. Beside it: 42,500 context switches per second against 12,000, and 7.9 cores busy against 7.2. At concurrency 4 the same lever is worth nothing (173 against 169 ms), because busy workers leave no idle time to spin through.

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS.why: deliberately NOT set, and it must be ABSENT rather than merely unset by us. The engine binds OpenBLAS to the thread budget at startup, and qwen_blas_set_threads() returns immediately when this variable is present -- so an unrelated export in the operating shell silently replaces the thread split this profile was qualified with, for every stage and every load. It would also disable the opt-in per-load adjustment (QWEN_SERVE_BLAS / QWEN_SERVE_BLAS_BUSY), which is off by default.
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS.revert: set it explicitly only to override the engine's own sizing, knowingly

QWEN_PREFIX_CACHE.why: reuses the request-independent prompt head; measured 9 of 13-79 positions on the production prompts

QWEN_SERVE_PROFILE.why: diagnostics; counters and timing never share a binary in a run that produces a number
QWEN_SERVE_PROFILE.revert: QWEN_SERVE_PROFILE=1 for the driver phase table

qualification.workload: NONE. Nothing here was measured on the machine you are about to run it on.
qualification.speaker: ryan
qualification.notes: Use this to START, then replace it. Two workers of eight threads is where a 16-core Arm host landed, and it rests on one measured fact that generalises -- a single request saturates at about eight threads and regresses at sixteen -- and one that does not: which topology wins depends on the concurrency you expect, because a worker only sees a batch at C >= 2W and the engine takes a different kernel above batch 2. Run the sweep in docs/serving-operations.md, then write your own profile with status 'qualified' and the numbers that earned it.
